bibliographic.title: Making AI Compliance Evidence Machine-Readable
bibliographic.authors: Rodrigo Cilla Ugarte; Miguel Ángel Patricio Guisado; Antonio Berlanga de Jesús; José Manuel Molina López
bibliographic.citation_apa: Cilla Ugarte, R., Patricio Guisado, M. Á., Berlanga de Jesús, A., & Molina López, J. M. (2024). Making AI compliance evidence machine-readable. Preprint submitted to IEEE Computer.

methodology.method_family: Compliance-as-Code technical framework with case validation
methodology.study_design: Architecture design and reference implementation validated on two Annex III high-risk AI systems
methodology.sample_description: Two high-risk systems under the EU AI Act: a credit scoring model and a medical imaging segmentation system
methodology.technology_context: OSCAL interchange format; three-layer Compliance-as-Code architecture (policy, evidence, enforcement); MLOps pipeline integration; EU AI Act, ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF

eligibility.decision_rationale: The paper strongly addresses AI governance, compliance evidence, risk traceability, auditability, and regulated high-risk contexts (EU AI Act Annex III), but the provided text contains no conversational systems, chatbots, agents, RAG, or LLM-specific governance. It is relevant as supporting infrastructure for machine-readable compliance and assurance, not as central evidence for conversational LLM governance.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial page 2 are available; confirm absence of conversational/LLM content in full text and verify empirical validation details, limitations, and peer-review status.

appraisal.notes: Clear problem statement and proposed architecture, but appraisal is limited by incomplete text. Validation on only two cases is acknowledged in abstract; detailed methods, results tables, limitations, and ethics discussion are not visible in the excerpt.

cerqual.explanation: The framework is internally coherent for AI compliance-as-code and regulated high-risk ML systems, but available evidence is partial and the work is not specific to conversational LLM governance. Two-case validation limits adequacy for broad synthesis claims.

coding.theme: Operationalizing AI governance through machine-readable compliance evidence
coding.subtheme: OSCAL-based Compliance-as-Code for high-risk AI systems
rq_alignment: human oversight (referenced via EU AI Act Articles 9–15)

synthesis.main_claim: AI governance frameworks specify what to assure but lack executable infrastructure; OSCAL can serve as a machine-readable interchange format for AI compliance, extended with 16 AI lifecycle properties and a three-layer Compliance-as-Code architecture that generates assurance evidence during model training.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes OSCAL extensions for AI lifecycle assurance, a policy-evidence-enforcement architecture, an SDK producing NIST-schema-validated OSCAL Assessment Results, and open-source validation on credit scoring and medical imaging high-risk systems.
synthesis.use_in_review: Include as supporting evidence for compliance, auditability, machine-readable governance artifacts, and regulated high-risk AI assurance. Do not use as central evidence for conversational LLM governance, guardrails, or dialogue-specific oversight mechanisms.
